symptom: `mxcli git merge p4 --plan` with "take": "theirs" on the conflicted Shop domain model committed a merge without Shop.OursOnly, an entity only ours had added and nobody conflicted on. The review listed it under Yours; nothing said the choice would drop it.
file: cmd/mxcli/cmd_git_merge.go wholeUnitDropReport / unitChanges / onlyIn; called in mergeRun's conflict stage and in applyPlan before the units are taken. Test: cmd/mxcli/gitmerge_whole_unit_drop_2325_test.go
cause: The plan resolves per unit by checking the chosen side's .mxunit out whole, so every change of the other side to that unit goes; the property report is per element and did not say the resolution is not.
insight: **The two mx diff files already hold the answer: a side's top-level change descriptions in a unit that the other side does not also list are exactly what taking the other side drops without a conflict.** Same description on both sides = the conflict itself (the choice), so it is not reported. The review prints both directions per unit before the plan is written; --plan prints only the chosen direction, before the commit. Element-level resolution (take per element) would need writing a merged unit, which the plan deliberately avoids (it checks a side's bytes out whole); warning is the honest scope. Live on 11.12.6 with real mx merge + mx diff: the review names Entity 'Shop.OursOnly' for theirs and 'Shop.TheirsOnly' for ours, and the theirs plan warns about OursOnly before 'Model merge committed'. Control: two sides changing only the same element report nothing.
